worker_memo:
# Advice: next work in Local Harness Lab

To: Maintainer · From: delegate advisor · Re: what to work on next

## Framing from the brief (known facts)

- The existing demonstration is adequately backed for the near-term horizon; the human is taking on rehearsal separately; the illustrative time budgets in #2's last comment (the "through Thursday, November 26" table) are not binding.
- Still binding: one shared GPU, scarce attentive review, and the value of useful work.
- Board state (ISSUES.md): 40 issues, 29 open, 11 closed. Open and un-parked (17): #2, #6, #7, #8, #10, #15, #18, #24, #25, #26, #28, #34, #35, #36, #37, #39, #40. Parked with explicit revisit conditions (12): #11, #19, #20, #21, #22, #27, #29, #30, #31, #32, #33, #38.

## First choice: #39 — count only reviewed acceptances in mixed Observatory campaign summaries

**Known facts.** `runOutcomeSummary` returns `2/2 accepted` on a verified two-row fixture where only one row carries `comparison_review: {status: "accepted"}` (issue body, board/39.md). Whether existing campaigns actually mix the schemas is explicitly unmeasured — that is a hypothesis, not a fact. The issue is labelled `worker-candidate`, has 0 comments, and refs #14 and #15. The body prescribes a bounded Worker slice: presentation-only change, an offline two-row Node regression test, preserved all-unreviewed and all-reviewed pending/operational-invalid behavior, raw scores and Python receipt binding left intact, and a before/after the Maintainer can verify with the same fixture. #15 (isolated Node evaluator) may reduce packaging cost but is not required for a host-side Node test.

**What decision it changes.** Whether a mixed-coverage campaign summary can be shown to a reader — rehearsal audience, or a public release — as an independent observation of what was accepted. Today such a summary overstates acceptance. It also removes one known defect from the inventory that #26 would otherwise have to classify, and it de-risks #34's outside-reader path (a published summary must not overclaim).

**Bounded first action.** Dispatch the Worker slice exactly as the issue body prescribes (fix + two-row Node regression test), then verify before/after on the fixture as the Maintainer. Zero GPU; review cost is one fixture diff plus the regression test.

**What would make me choose a different issue.**
- If a reader-facing campaign actually displays mixed-coverage rows, #39 moves from "known latent defect" to "active misstatement" — fix first, no further evidence needed. If the Maintainer checks and no current demo campaign mixes the schemas, urgency drops and #26 or #34 moves up.
- If the owner wants to publish now (a link the listener can open unaided), #34 comes first, per #2's own table row.
- If a claim about what was independently observed is disputed, #26's one-task audit moves ahead, per #2's comment.

## Alternative 1: #26 — audit what independent evidence backs evaluator results and cleanup receipts

Same evidence-integrity axis, broader. Read-only inventory of one task and one command lifecycle; mark each signal's source (candidate process, separate reader of output data, outer memory scope, inner per-command scope). Known starting points from the body: SQLite already has a separate data observer; some Event checks have imported candidate code; the outer job has a cgroup-empty-or-absent check. CPU-only, zero GPU, no label, 0 comments.

Why it is a real alternative: it is the upstream question of which #39 is a symptom, and #2's comment names it as the move when a claim about independent observation is disputed. Why it ranks below #39: the issue itself says to "identify any remaining ambiguity before adding machinery," so the deliverable is an inventory plus improving one independently observable result — less bounded, and it costs more review attention per unit of reader-facing value than a verified one-function fix.

## Alternative 2: #34 — prepare the repository for public release and verify an outside-reader path

The remaining "separate objective" from #2's comment: a shareable public URL. Scope: choose a license with the owner, inventory upstream code/fixtures/notices (mini-SWE-agent adaptations, CPython-derived tasks), scan tracked tree, reachable history, issue/comment text and CI artifacts for private material, and rehearse one public-reader path without private bulk storage. Close after an owner-approved visibility change and a logged-out clone/walkthrough check.

Why it is a real alternative: the brief says the demonstration is adequately backed for the near-term horizon and rehearsal is taken off the Maintainer's plate, so the public-URL objective is the main remaining near-term value beyond engineering. Why it ranks third: it is owner-gated (license choice, approval, history review; full cost unknown per #2's table), so the Maintainer cannot unilaterally start the critical path, and the #35 split can wait — #34's own comment says "Publication can precede the split," and #35's body says "Keep #34 able to ship first."

## Why the rest rank lower

- **GPU-bound or parked**: all 12 parked issues — #11, #19, #20, #21, #22, #27, #29, #30, #31, #32, #33, #38 — carry the `parked` label with named revisit conditions. #2's decision rule says to name an outcome that would change a recipe, deployment, claim or investigation and price both GPU occupancy and review before spending; none of them currently names one. The 150-confirmation history (132 full acceptances, 5 source failures, 13 handoff-only failures, ~4 h 48 min serial) is the concrete cost of broad confirmation, and a fresh reviewer plus the Maintainer both favor deferring a repeat ladder screen (#2 comment, 2026-11-18T18:17:04Z).
- **#15 (isolated Node evaluator)**: the issue itself says to use one more real assignment before broadening; #39's host-side Node test does not need it.
- **#18 (portable replay)**: was #2's first engineering choice "if independent inspection of another case matters"; the brief says the demonstration is adequately backed for the near-term horizon, so that condition no longer binds.
- **#10, #24, #25, #28, #36, #37, #40**: real but lower value; #40 (root-relative link repair) is a cheap worker-candidate that could ride along with a #39 dispatch, not a primary pick. #36 (reproducible Ruff) and #37 (opt-in pre-commit hooks) are small developer-workflow chores that #8's ty pilot already pulls toward, so they follow #8 rather than leading it.

## How the historical record shaped this ranking

- **Closed outcomes**: #17 closed with two prospectively timed assignments and a task-selection rule; its final comment explicitly points at #39 — "the mixed-summary counter case in #39 offers a reusable Node oracle" — and found "little reason to elevate #11: most measured effort was outside dispatch." That demotes #11 and supplies the review-cost evidence for #39 (a reusable oracle, verifiable counterexamples). #16 closed with two fresh comparison blocks and the Aider history-allowance fix (2048→8192, warm verified time 185.6→156.2 s); its note that "Worker was considerably slower" on the issue-selection block is a caution against adding more comparison runs before the evidence-integrity work is done.
- **Labels**: `worker-candidate` on #39 and #40 marks them as dispatch-ready slices; the 12 `parked` labels with revisit conditions are treated as deferred, not queued, per #2's suggested parked semantics.
- **Cross-links**: #39 refs #14 and #15; #14's rejected submission (artifact failed two independent probes) is the template for the kind of counterexample a #39 regression test should preserve. #34↔#35 cross-link resolves to "#34 can ship first." #2's candidate table is the only place that prices #18/#26/#39/#34 against each other, and its conditions (audience access, evidence needs) are exactly what the brief has now changed.

## Known facts vs hypotheses

- Facts: the #39 two-row fixture defect and its prescribed slice; #26's scope and starting points; #34's owner-gated scope and the #35-can-wait comments; #17's and #16's closed outcomes as recorded; board label and comment text cited above.
- Hypotheses: that no current reader-facing campaign mixes the schemas (unmeasured per #39); that #39's fix is worth a Worker dispatch rather than a direct Maintainer edit (the issue's worker-candidate label and #17's reusable-oracle note support it, but the Maintainer's own time is the final arbiter); that the owner is available for the #34 license/disclosure decisions on the near-term horizon.

Raw result files and uncopied targets were unavailable in this packet; all citations above are to ISSUES.md, the board files, and the linked documents present in the repo.
outer_before_worker:
First pick #39. A two-row fixture already demonstrates a decision-facing defect: one reviewed acceptance and one raw pass can display as two acceptances. Determine prevalence on saved campaign details separately, then fix the mixed summary and exercise the all-reviewed/no-review boundaries via actual JS. Do directly if packaging consumes the whole edit. Use this real UI assignment to see whether #15 now earns its isolated Node integration cost. Stop after the focused fix and give prevalence honestly; skip general Node work if it provides no repeatable benefit.
Next #26, a bounded audit of one evaluator observation and one command closure. Move it first if a real workflow consumes an ambiguous independent correctness or cleanup claim, or acceptance expands. A fixture-only UI defect and a strategic audit answer different questions.
Third, consider the offline portion of parked #19: #23 supplied four serial same-recipe jobs with separated dispatch/task costs. Look at already-recorded phase durations and how often we actually batch. Run no new jobs or resident backend prototype unless the removable part changes a real workload decision. The unusually slow first launch is not representative by itself.
#32 is topical but first decide if held-out second reading can save scarce review on failures of this sort; two of the three #23 rejections concern material in the review artifact. #18 or #34 returns to the front if a real reader needs a portable replay or outside access. Dinner rehearsal is the user's, existing demo is covered. #40 is a good training assignment with little marginal engineering payoff. No automatic broad reliability screen.
outer_update_before_reading_memo: The pre-memo prevalence check found no mixed runs among 396 qualifying historical records. Downgrade #39 to small opportunistic repair. Favor #26, initially one task and one command lifecycle: establish who actually observes the persisted behavior and the cleanup being claimed. A separate candidate, #19, now has a real phase bound from four same-recipe jobs: only about 35 s of the 450 s sequence came from later model loads, retaining the initial load. Inspect demand on other batches before a residency change. No reason to spend more inference to get those numbers.

decision.assessment: Useful independent shortlist and an explicit reversal condition. The counts and label sets match the frozen board. Worker correctly distinguished the mixed-summary fixture from unknown historical exposure, understood that #39 can be fixed without #15, and that publication can precede #35. The full advice is unsuitable to follow verbatim: dispatching local Worker does require the GPU, #17's reusable-oracle suggestion was an interim comment, and #36 explicitly says its lint work can advance separately from #8. The final #17 comment prioritizes tasks with substantial work left after specification. Neither party had to propose #39 independently of the board: earlier priorities and links were visible.
decision.trace: 42 tool calls, three context resets, first durable memo at approximately 159 s on the nominal agent clock, and 359 s of agent time through submission. Late checks correctly tested board tallies and memberships. They did not establish attribution, cost or dependencies. One advisory job gives no model-wide estimate.
decision.recommendation: Work #26 next. The fixture in #39 deserves a bounded fix, but the Maintainer found zero mixed comparison-review statuses in the 396 stored non-delegated multi-trial campaigns examined, ten of which had any comparison-review status. Transient live exposure is unknown. Start #26 with one Event persistence result and one command cleanup receipt; identify the process or data source behind each claim. Use the separate SQLite reader as a comparison. Stop with one replayed improvement or a precise qualification if the existing evidence suffices.
decision.alternatives: #39 moves back up if a live mixed run misstates acceptance or a nearby Observatory change makes the fix cheap. #34 moves first when an actual outside reader needs public access and the owner is ready for the release decisions. #19 has a cheap offline follow-up: eliminating only the three subsequent model loads in #23's batch would save about 35 s of 450 s of serial dispatch. The first 84 s load remains; this is a load-only bound for that batch. No prototype or new model screen is warranted by that number alone.
